A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RDSMC research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material across appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling experiments on Gaussian mixtures, Rings, Funnel and four Bayesian logistic regression datasets, with additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds computational-budget comparisons, runtime measurements and a PDDS comparison in Appendix E.5.

M1.justification: The outer RDSMC construction is retained, but v2 adds an optional rejection-sampling estimator in Algorithm 4. Algorithm 3 also changes substantively: after aligning indices, v1 applies an MCMC transition targeting the preceding annealing distribution, whereas v2 targets the next distribution before applying the weight ratio. Whether this printed revision changed implementation is unresolved. AIS itself was already used in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Gaussian mixtures, Rings, Funnel and Bayesian logistic regression on Credit, Cancer, Ionosphere and Sonar. The added experiments revisit this coverage under different computational settings and metrics; they introduce no new dataset or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated Particle Denoising Diffusion Sampler (PDDS) comparator on Funnel in Appendix E.5.3; v1 only discussed this method as related work. The original AIS, SMC, SMS, RDMC and SLIPS comparisons remain. Moving existing baseline curves into Figure 1 does not add comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix E.5 introduces a substantial additional evaluation protocol: fixed RDSMC inner-sampling budgets, adaptive MALA, aligned diffusion-sampler budgets, and approximately runtime-matched AIS/SMC configurations initialized without target-variance information. Regression additionally uses LPPD for validation and testing. These are new experimental settings alongside the retained main experiments, not same-setting performance updates.

E4.justification: v2 adds computational-budget and initialization-controlled comparisons across the existing targets, together with runtime analyses separating initialization costs. These examine whether the original comparisons depend on unequal computational resources or privileged initialization. It also reports sensitivity to the resampling start time on Rings. The original Proposal and IS ablations remain.

E5.justification: The retained main results still use five seeds and standard errors. The new controlled experiments and PDDS evaluation report ten seeds; Figure 3 uses two-standard-error runtime bars. This adds statistical reporting for new experiments without establishing additional runs for the retained results. Confidence-interval-overlap highlighting already existed in v1.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1 and 2 retain their values, but v2 adds runtime results, controlled-comparison scores and LPPD results in Figures 3–4 and Tables 7–8. For example, the new protocol gives RDSMC Funnel sliced KSD of 0.075±0.005. PDDS results are also added. Conversely, v1 Table 5's unique Rings Wasserstein and angle-TVD results disappear.

T1.justification: The main theorems, regularity assumptions and Appendix C proofs are substantially retained; Observations 1–2 restate existing marginal identities. Appendix B.1.3 adds an unbiasedness assertion for the new rejection-based marginal estimator. However, Algorithm 4's C*M/M_total estimator is generally biased under its stopping rule of collecting M acceptances, leaving this theoretical extension problematic.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the central claims: training-free diffusion-based SMC, intermediate targets obtained from score-estimation byproducts, asymptotically exact sampling, unbiased normalization-constant estimation and competitive empirical performance. Revised terminology and additional supporting experiments do not substantially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 expands the twisting-function and bias-correction explanations. It also interprets the new comparisons through initialization and runtime differences, restricts recommended Rings resampling settings after observing instability, and cautions that PDDS timings use different hardware and software. Existing limitations concerning mode collapse, auxiliary variance and oracle tuning are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an RDSMC code-access link, identifies the PyTorch implementation, and supplies detailed recommended settings and an adaptive-step-size rule. Tables 5–6 document selected resampling thresholds and runtime-matched baseline configurations. PDDS hardware, framework and training/sampling times are also disclosed. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's existing grids and hardware description.

R1.justification: A new Appendix D substantially develops the relationship to Twisted Diffusion Sampler through shared twisting weights, different targets and auxiliary randomness. v2 also integrates He, Rojas and Tao's rejection-based sampling work throughout the methodological positioning, while removing Chen et al.'s Sequential Controlled Langevin Diffusions from the closest-prior-work discussion and bibliography.

P1.justification: The introduction, background and method exposition are extensively rewritten, with revised terminology, a dedicated notation paragraph and named observations. Appendix B is reorganized around estimation, complexity and implementation guidance, and a dedicated prior-method comparison separates it from the experimental appendix. These changes extend beyond merely inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 merges the previously separate full-baseline GMM comparison into Figure 1 and redraws existing GMM plots with logarithmic dimension axes. It adds runtime and controlled-result figures plus four new settings/results tables, while removing v1's additional Rings table. The principal visual changes involve consolidation, redesigned axes and substantial new displays.

improvement.justification: The controlled comparisons, LPPD evaluation and implementation guidance substantially strengthen empirical scrutiny and reproducibility. However, v2 removes Rings diagnostics and introduces estimator correctness concerns: Algorithm 3 changes the transition target without a corresponding weighting adjustment, and Algorithm 4 asserts unbiasedness for a generally biased stopped-sampling ratio. The PDFs do not resolve whether the AIS discrepancy is textual or implemented. These benefits and harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
